- This means that the measure of $∠CAD$ must be the *difference* between the large angle $(∠BAD)$ and the smaller known angle $(∠BAC).$

Therefore,

$$
x={100}^{∘}-{70}^{∘}={30}^{∘}.
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
When two angles share a common side, they are called **adjacent** angles. When two angles are adjacent, we can add their measures to find the measure of the larger angle. 

For example, consider the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131900/assets/f562f3505de0dd2345b29e2baabaf51a7885cbccb5d95e6201b8bc9aec1b1986.png)

The angles $\angle PSR$ and $\angle RST$ are adjacent because they both have the side $\overrightarrow{SR}$ in common.

Since the angles $\angle PSR$ and $\angle RST$ are adjacent, we can find the measure of the combined angle $\angle PST$ by adding the two angles:

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠PST & ={{m∠PSR}_{⏟}}_{\text{orange angle}}+{{m∠RST}_{⏟}}_{\text{blue angle}} \\  & ={95}^{∘}+{45}^{∘} \\  & ={140}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Extending the Sums of Angles Rule
tutorials.problem:
We can extend our rule relating sums of adjacent angles to more than two angles.

For example, let's consider the angles shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14131900/assets/3264d0ab1a40b02915a737dad57e9f26820193d9bdc6b42431ec1ab6508cc523.png)

According to our rule, the measure of the reflex angle $\angle QST$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠QST & ={{m∠QSP}_{⏟}}_{\text{green angle}}+{{m∠PSR}_{⏟}}_{\text{orange angle}}+{{m∠RST}_{⏟}}_{\text{blue angle}} \\  & ={100}^{∘}+{95}^{∘}+{45}^{∘} \\  & ={240}^{∘}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can also use this rule to determine the size of a smaller angle when we know a larger one. Let's see an example.
